summary: The Syrian Supreme Court sentenced former President Bashar al-Assad to death on charges including murder, mass murder, child abuse, torture, and deprivation of liberty, with six former military officials also convicted. Simultaneously, Israel's IDF Unit 99 identified and eliminated a Hamas scout near the Yellow Line in Gaza. In Lebanon, the parliament abolished capital punishment, replacing it with life imprisonment. Additional developments include an Israeli strike on civilian homes in southern Lebanon, a rocket attack on Kfar Rumman in Iraq, revelations about Mossad visits to Iran's Fordow nuclear site, and ongoing US-Fordow nuclear negotiations.
key_points: The Syrian Supreme Court sentenced former President Bashar al-Assad to death on charges including murder, mass murder, child abuse, torture, and deprivation of liberty, with six former military officials also convicted (Source: @VahidOnline/77814).
Israel's IDF Unit 99 identified a Hamas scout near the Yellow Line in Gaza and immediately eliminated the threat (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/384114).
Israeli forces detonated homes in Beit Yahun, southern Lebanon, under IDF control following a recent explosion (Source: @sharghdaily/177505).
Lebanon's parliament abolished the death penalty, replacing it with life imprisonment, marking a historic legislative change (Source: @mamlekate/104127).
A rocket attack was launched on Kfar Rumman in Iraq, resulting in casualties among local forces (Source: @redlinkleb/35931).
Former Mossad chief Yossi Cohen disclosed that Israeli intelligence visited Iran's Fordow nuclear site multiple times between 2016 and 2021 to study the facility (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6227).
Intelligence indicates US officials are pursuing negotiations regarding the Fordow nuclear site amid ongoing tensions in the region (Source: @amitsegal/63802).
